clue.text: Get going, as a chorus girl does?

definitions.meaning: an old military call to rise from bed, meaning get up and start moving
a high-kicking chorus line dancer displays a limb on stage

explanation.surface: A dancer is told to get moving.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a wake-up idiom for rising and starting work, and literally describes a dancer's display of a limb.

clue.text: Anti-Winfrey slogan raised, a deadly shaft

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a protest against the TV host Oprah Winfrey might read NO OPRAH

explanation.surface: A protest banner against a TV host is held up, like a lethal spear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns NO OPRAH upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A whaler's barbed spear is thrown as a lethal shaft.

clue.text: Campaign to repress one enchanting country sport

parts.note: a witch is one who casts enchantments
fox hunting is a traditional English country sport

explanation.surface: A drive against dissenters is likened to a charming rural pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: A persecution campaign against people with unpopular views is named after the old hounding of supposed sorcerers.

clue.text: Left, having finished as partner

parts.note: something finished is over

explanation.surface: Someone left behind after a relationship ended.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic partner is a sweetheart or paramour.

clue.text: Animal, valuable, likely to fetch a lot

parts.note: gold is valuable, so golden can describe something precious
a retriever is a dog bred to fetch shot game, and one that fetches a lot

explanation.surface: A pricey creature expected to sell well at auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fetch a lot' reads as an auction price, but it means a dog bringing things back.
explanation.definitionFit: This popular breed of gun dog is an animal.

clue.text: Mature, on the way to get badge of rank

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the other piece

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
ripe means mature

explanation.surface: Seasoned and en route to promotion insignia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mature' looks like the start of a description of an officer, but it is a plain synonym; 'on' places it after the street abbreviation in this across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevron or band sewn on a sleeve shows military rank.

clue.text: So promiscuous a woman is an outlaw

definitions.meaning: a ... woman is a promiscuous one, so the colour word describes her
Will ... is one of Robin Hood's band of outlaws in English legend

explanation.surface: A loose woman is cast as a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: Will Scarlet is one of Robin Hood's Merry Men, outlaws of Sherwood Forest in English folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: The red colour labels a fallen woman in the phrase about promiscuity, and is the surname of a Merry Man.

clue.text: Prepared to bowl, as cricket score mounted

definitions.meaning: a cricket bowler's approach before delivering the ball
runs piled up, so the score was ...

explanation.surface: A bowler gets set while the batting side's total climbs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler's approach is the run-up, and to run up a score is to accumulate runs.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a bowler's approach; the phrasal verb means accumulated a total.

clue.text: Looking sulky, getting pressure to go on excursion

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece goes on top of the second

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
an outing is an excursion

explanation.surface: A child sulks when pushed to join a day trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing out the lips is the classic sullen expression.

clue.text: Horrible youth runs through club

indicators.note: the letter for runs passes into the middle of the club

parts.note: a bat is a club
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A yob charges at someone wielding a club.
explanation.definitionFit: An unruly, badly behaved child is a horrible youngster.

clue.text: Criminal stashes nothing in house in America

indicators.note: the house-in-America phrase hides the zero inside it, as a stash

parts.note: a villa is a house
taken as written
US is short for United States
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A crook hides loot in a property in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stashes' tells you the house-in-America phrase swallows the zero, which lands just before the final two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicked, lawbreaking act is felonious.

clue.text: Reassuring news from family in Scottish town

parts.note: mother is a family member
being well is reassuring health news

explanation.surface: Relatives send comforting word from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'Mother well', a reassuring report from home.
explanation.definitionFit: This Lanarkshire town near Glasgow is known for its football club.

clue.text: In bedsit, I feed

indicators.note: the I goes inside the word for a bedsit

parts.note: a pad is slang for a small flat or bedsit

explanation.surface: A lodger eats in their bedsit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feed' is read as fee'd, given a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as fee'd, the definition means remunerated, settled with a fee.

clue.text: Tobacco from tin not burning

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
a fire that has gone out is not burning

explanation.surface: Cigarette tobacco kept in a tin, unlit.
explanation.walkthrough: SNOUT is British prison slang for tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: British prison slang uses this nose word for tobacco or cigarettes.

clue.text: Blown up, trail grew wild

indicators.note: wild signals the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A path in the wild has become overgrown and magnified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges TRAIL GREW.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes something magnified or shown on a bigger scale.

clue.text: Sucker appearing in spring

parts.note: a dupe who is tricked on the first day of a spring month

explanation.surface: A plant shoot pops up in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' looks like a plant shoot, but it is a gullible person fooled on 1 April.
explanation.definitionFit: The victim of a prank on the first of the fourth month is a dupe in spring.

clue.text: It's lucky our strong point is catching fish

indicators.note: the strong point word holds the fish inside it, as if it had caught it

parts.note: a forte is one's strong point
a tuna is a fish

explanation.surface: An angler boasts that hooking fish is a happy skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Being favoured by chance is being blessed with good luck.

clue.text: Do a nice dance as a nymph

indicators.note: dance means the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A water sprite is asked to perform a pleasant dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dance' rearranges DO A NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a sea nymph, a daughter of Oceanus, bears this name.

clue.text: Confidently tipping how one may be caught

definitions.meaning: a nap is a racing tipster's most confident selection
to be caught asleep is to be caught off guard

explanation.surface: A tipster boldly picks a horse and is caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: In British horse racing a nap is a tipster's best bet of the day; 'caught napping' means caught unawares.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipsters name a confident racing pick a nap; dozing is also how someone is caught off guard.

clue.text: Sense of satisfaction after quiet journey

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: Contentment after a peaceful trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling pleased at an achievement is a glow of self-esteem.

clue.text: Swells and dies horribly

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters are mangled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something bloats and then expires gruesomely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' rearranges AND DIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Swells is old slang for fashionable men, fops.

clue.text: Alter westward course of german border river

indicators.note: in an across clue, going westward means reading right to left

parts.note: the Oder forms much of the border between Germany and Poland

explanation.surface: A river on the German frontier changes its direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'westward course of' turns ODER backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something over is to change or revise it.

clue.text: Who believes daggers may be concealed?

indicators.note: the letters are held inside the words Who believes, as if concealed

explanation.surface: Asking which faithful person might carry hidden knives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed' points to the run inside whO BELIeves.
explanation.definitionFit: Obelus is the printers' name for the dagger mark, plural obeli.

clue.text: Puzzled after sharp tip gets blunt

indicators.note: the puzzled word comes after the sharp tip word

parts.note: a point is a sharp tip
a blank look is a puzzled one

explanation.surface: A bewildered person finds a sharp tip gone dull.
explanation.definitionFit: A forthright remark made directly is frank and to the point.

clue.text: Present programme on radio

definitions.meaning: the present is this current day
the flagship BBC Radio 4 morning news show

explanation.surface: A gift is announced in a radio show.
explanation.walkthrough: Today is BBC Radio 4's long-running morning news programme.
explanation.definitionFit: The present time is this day; the BBC morning news show carries the name.

clue.text: Wretchedly endure evil without end

indicators.note: wretchedly signals the letters are put into a poor, disordered state

explanation.surface: Someone suffers miserably from never-ending wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wretchedly' rearranges ENDURE EVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never eased or broken is ceaseless, with no respite.

clue.text: In memorial service, nothing was painful

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
bit, past tense of bite, as cold or a sting bites

explanation.surface: At a funeral, nothing hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: An obit was historically a mass or service held for the dead on an anniversary.

clue.text: Planting privet, say, but not at the front in border

indicators.note: the opening letter of the gardening word is removed

parts.note: privet is a shrub commonly planted for hedges, so planting it is hedging

explanation.surface: A gardener plants a privet line along the edge of a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not at the front' removes the H from HEDGING.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative trim or margin is a fringe.

clue.text: Ulster Protestant, initially changing sides, remains monarchy supporter

indicators.note: the first letter swaps left for right, the two sides

parts.note: a loyalist in Northern Ireland supports union with Britain, usually a Protestant

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish unionist switches allegiance but stays loyal to the Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially changing sides' swaps the opening L (left) for R (right) in LOYALIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of the crown backs kings and queens.
